title: Preterite — Irregular Verbs
description: Learn the high-frequency irregular preterite verbs: ESTAR, IR, HACER, TENER, and DECIR.

grammar.title: Irregular Past Participles
grammar.content:
Several common verbs have irregular past participles that must be memorized:

- abrir → abierto (opened)
- cubrir → cubierto (covered)
- devolver → devuelto (returned)
- escribir → escrito (written)
- hacer → hecho (done/made)
- morir → muerto (died)
- poner → puesto (put/placed)
- romper → roto (broken)
- resolver → resuelto (resolved)
- ver → visto (seen)
- volver → vuelto (returned)
- disolver → disuelto (dissolved)
examples: He abierto la ventana. (I have opened the window.)
¿Has escrito el correo? (Have you written the email?)
Ya he hecho la tarea. (I've already done the homework.)
Ella ha visto esa película. (She has seen that movie.)
grammar.aid_note: Note that irregular participles follow the same grammar rules as regular ones when combined with haber: 'He hecho' (I have done), 'He visto' (I have seen). The irregularity is only in the participle form itself.

grammar.title: Other Common Irregulars: DORMIR, PODER, SABER, QUERER, VENIR
grammar.content:
These verbs have stem changes in the preterite (third person only), similar to the present tense stem changes but applied differently:

- DORMIR (o→ue): durmió, durmieron
- PODER (o→ue): pudo, pudieron
- SABER (regular stem but irregular meaning): supe, supiste, supo, supimos, supisteis, supieron
- QUERER (e→ie): quiso, quisieron
- VENIR (vino, vinieron):

These only change in the third person (él/ella/usted and ellos/ellas/ustedes). The first and second persons follow regular patterns.
examples: Ella durmió ocho horas. (She slept eight hours.)
No pude ir al cine. (I couldn't go to the cinema.)
¿Supiste la noticia? (Did you learn the news?)
No quiso comer. (He/She didn't want to eat.)
Ellos vinieron a visitarnos. (They came to visit us.)
grammar.aid_note: DORMIR has an additional twist: the 'i' in durmió/durmieron sounds like a 'y' — 'durmió' is pronounced 'durió'. This is a common feature in Spanish when 'i' follows another vowel: 'viene' (comes) → 'vino' (came), pronounced 'vin-o'.

grammar.title: Present Perfect — Haber + Past Participle
grammar.content:
The present perfect is formed with the present tense of haber + a past participle. It's used to talk about actions that happened in the recent past or that have relevance to the present.

Haber conjugation (present tense):
- yo: he
- tú: has
- él/ella/usted: ha
- nosotros: hemos
- vosotros: habéis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: han

The past participle is formed by:
- -AR verbs: drop -ar, add -ado (hablar → hablado)
- -ER verbs: drop -er, add -ido (comer → comido)
- -IR verbs: drop -ir, add -ido (vivir → vivido)
examples: Hoy he comido paella. (Today I have eaten paella.)
¿Has visto la televisión esta semana? (Have you watched TV this week?)
Hemos vivido aquí dos años. (We have lived here for two years.)
Mi amigo ha trabajado mucho. (My friend has worked a lot.)
grammar.aid_note: In most of Spain, the present perfect is used for recent past (today, this week, this month). In Latin America, the simple preterite is often preferred even for recent events. Both are correct — the regional usage differs. Think of 'he comido' as 'I have eaten' vs 'comí' as 'I ate.'

grammar.title: Preterite (Pretérito Indefinido) — Regular Verbs
grammar.content:
The preterite tense is used to talk about completed actions in the past with a clear beginning or end. Think of it as the 'storytelling' tense — you're telling someone what happened.

For regular -AR verbs (like hablar), the endings are:
- yo: -é
- tú: -aste
- él/ella/usted: -ó
- nosotros: -amos
- vosotros: -asteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -aron

For regular -ER/-IR verbs (like comer, vivir), the endings are:
- yo: -í
- tú: -iste
- él/ella/usted: -ió
- nosotros: -imos
- vosotros: -isteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -ieron
examples: Ayer hablé con mi amigo. (Yesterday I talked with my friend.)
Ellos comieron pizza anoche. (They ate pizza last night.)
Nosotros vivimos en Madrid dos años. (We lived in Madrid for two years.)
¿Estudiaste para el examen? (Did you study for the exam?)
grammar.aid_note: Watch out: 'nosotros' form looks the same for -AR preterite and present! Context tells you which: 'hablamos' in present = we speak; 'hablamos' in preterite = we spoke. Look for time words like 'ayer' (yesterday), 'la semana pasada' (last week).

grammar.title: Preterite — High-Frequency Irregular Verbs (ESTAR, IR, HACER, TENER, DECIR)
grammar.content:
These five verbs share the same irregular stem in the preterite: tuv-, estuv-, hic-, dij-. IR has its own pattern (fui-, fuiste-...). They all drop the accent on nosotros.

The shared irregular endings (for ESTAR, HACER, TENER, DECIR) are:
- yo: -e
- tú: -iste
- él/ella/usted: -o
- nosotros: -imos (no accent)
- vosotros: -isteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -ieron

IR uses the same endings but with its own unique stems:
- yo: fui
- tú: fuiste
- él/ella/usted: fue
- nosotros: fuimos
- vosotros: fuisteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: fueron
examples: Ayer estuve en el parque. (Yesterday I was at the park.)
El año pasado fui a Italia. (Last year I went to Italy.)
Ella hizo la cena. (She made dinner.)
Tuvimos un buen día. (We had a good day.)
Juan dijo la verdad. (Juan told the truth.)
grammar.aid_note: IR (to go) and ESTAR (to be) have the SAME preterite forms. Context determines meaning: 'Ayer fui al cine' (I went to the cinema) vs 'Ayer estuve en el cine' (I was at the cinema). Both are correct but slightly different meanings.

pronunciation.title: Irregular Preterite — Stress Patterns
pronunciation.content:
Irregular preterite verbs (estar, ir, hacer, tener, decir, poner, salir, venir, saber, querer, dormir, poder) have **accented endings**:

1. **Yo form** always has an accent mark:
   - estuve = es-TOO-veh (stress on 'tooh')
   - fui = fwee (one syllable)
   - hice = EE-seh (stress on 'ee')
   - tuve = TOO-veh (stress on 'tuu')
   - dije = DEE-heh (stress on 'dee')
   - puse = POOS-eh (stress on 'poo')
   - salí = sah-LEE (stress on 'lee')
   - vine = VEEN-eh (stress on 'veen')
   - supe = SOO-peh (stress on 'suu')
   - quise = KEES-eh (stress on 'kee')
   - dormí = dor-MEE (stress on 'mee')
   - pude = POO-deh (stress on 'poo')

The accent marks are the key — they always mark the stressed syllable in these irregular forms.

pronunciation.title: Stem Vowel Changes
pronunciation.content:
Irregular preterites often change their stem vowel:

1. **e → i** (stem change): decir → dije, pedir → pedí
   - The 'i' is always a clear 'ee' sound
2. **o → u** (stem change): poder → pude, dormir → dormí
   - The 'u' is always 'oo' as in 'food'
3. **u → u** (no change): poner → puse
   - The 'u' is always 'oo'

In the third person plural (ellos/ellas):
- estuvieron = es-too-VEH-ron (stress on 'VEH')
- estuvieron = es-too-VEH-ron (stress on 'VEH')
- hicieron = ee-see-EH-ron (stress on 'EH')
- tuvieron = too-vee-EH-ron (stress on 'EH')
- dijeron = dee-HEH-ron (stress on 'HEH')

pronunciation.title: Irregular Preterite — Vowel Harmony in Stems
pronunciation.content:
Many irregular preterite verbs have stem vowels that follow patterns:

1. **-IR verbs with stem change (dormir → durmió)**: O → U in 3rd person singular
   - durmió = door-MEE-oh (stress on 'mee', not 'dor')
2. **-ER/-IR verbs with 'yo' form ending in -je**: decir → dije = DEE-heh
3. **tener/tener → tuve**: stress on 'tu' — TOOH-veh (not TOOH-vee)
4. **estar/estar → estuve**: es-TU-veh (stress on 'tu')
5. **hacer/hacer → hice**: EES-eh (the 'c' before 'e' = 's' sound)

Key pronunciation pattern: The 3rd person singular (él/ella/usted) of -IR stem-changing verbs drops the 'i' and adds an accent:
- dormir → durmió = door-MEE-oh (not door-MEE-roh)
- servir → sirvió = seer-VEE-oh
- pedir → pidió = peh-DEE-oh

examples.source: DEE-hoh (the 'j' = strong 'h' sound, not 'j' like English)

exercises.question: What is the preterite of 'estar' for 'yo'?
exercises.explanation: 'Estuve' is the irregular preterite of estar for yo. The stem changes to estuv-.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ella ____ (decir) la verdad ayer.' (She told the truth yesterday.)
exercises.explanation: 'Dijo' is the irregular preterite of decir for él/ella/usted. The stem changes to dij-.

exercises.question: Complete: '¿____ (haber) ____ (you) comido?' (Have you eaten?)
exercises.explanation: '¿Has comido?' is the present perfect: tú form of haber (has) + past participle (comido).

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the correct preterite irregular?
exercises.explanation: 'Tuvo' is the correct preterite form. Note the accent on the o — it follows the rule for words ending in a vowel (stress on 2nd-to-last by default).

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ayer ____ (ir) al supermercado.' (Yesterday I went to the supermarket.)
exercises.explanation: 'Fui' is the irregular preterite of ir for yo. IR and ESTAR share the same preterite conjugations.

exercises.question: What is the irregular past participle of 'hacer'?
exercises.explanation: 'Hecho' is the irregular past participle of hacer. Used in present perfect: 'He hecho' (I have done).

exercises.question: Complete the preterite tense conjugation table for the irregular verb HACER:
exercises.explanation: Hacer is irregular in the preterite (hic- stem): hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron.
